artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation of markdown-safe, title-aware, word-boundary truncation at both slice sites in generate-task-order.sh, with a new 16-assertion regression suite, live-data verification, and a render-side-parity port to the .opencode/ mirror.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed both blind character-slice sites in generate-task-order.sh's Grouped by Topic summary lines: the source expression now prefers .title over .description, strips inline-markup hazard characters before slicing, and truncates on a word boundary with a visible marker reserved within budget; the cross-topic short_desc slice shares the same guarantees via a new idempotent bash helper. Added a 16-assertion regression suite (proven red against the pre-fix script, green after), deployed, regenerated specs/TODO.md against live data with full line-by-line verification, and ported the fix to the .opencode/ renderer mirror. Full gate set (79-suite shell test run, task-reference lint, deploy-freshness) all green.

memory_candidates.content: For a truncate-to-budget-with-word-boundary-and-marker requirement that must be applied at more than one slice site (e.g. a primary render plus a shortened secondary annotation derived from the same field), implement it once per language needed (a jq `def` and a bash function) with IDENTICAL semantics: reserve the marker's length WITHIN the stated budget (cut = budget - marker_len, not budget + marker_len), back off to the last word boundary at-or-before that cut point, and make the bash helper idempotent against an already-marked input (strip a trailing marker before re-cutting) so a value already truncated by the primary slice is never double-marked when a smaller secondary budget cuts it again. Never open-code the same truncation logic a second time at a second site -- that is exactly how the original defect this pattern fixes was introduced.

Adding a new scripts/tests/test-*.sh file under any extension in agent-system/extensions/ requires registering it in that extension's own manifest.json `provides.scripts` array, or the next deploy fails doc-lint with `FAIL: script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts: <path>` even though the file itself is syntactically fine and passes when run directly. This is easy to miss because the test suite itself runs correctly pre-deploy (run-all.sh discovers it via glob, no registration needed there) -- the registration is a doc-lint/deploy-time requirement, not a test-discovery requirement, so a suite can be written, pass locally, and still break the next deploy-headless.sh run until the manifest entry is added.

general-implementation-agent (and any implement-stage agent) must NEVER call update-task-status.sh directly to transition a task's status to completed -- that is the orchestrator's own postflight job, performed AFTER the agent returns and its .return-meta.json (status: implemented, never completed) is read. Calling it directly prematurely flips specs/state.json and regenerates specs/TODO.md (and, via update-phase-status.sh's own mechanism, can touch the plan's plan-level Status field too), which can desync from what the orchestrator's postflight then expects to do itself (completion_data propagation, roadmap linking, memory-candidate harvesting). If this happens, it can be cleanly undone with zero collateral damage by restoring specs/state.json from `git show HEAD:specs/state.json` (never hand-edit JSON with Python's json.dump on this file without `ensure_ascii=False` -- the default escapes every non-ASCII character like em-dashes into \uXXXX sequences, corrupting every OTHER task's description field in a giant unwanted diff), re-applying only the single targeted field via `jq`, regenerating TODO.md, and reverting the plan file's Status line with Edit.
